rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (score 347): the oval now finishes 15 of 20 trials (progress 0.94, mean time 1.69 s), so the change to a wider sensor spread, lower kp and higher kd worked on smooth bends. The s-bend (progress 0.42) and slalom (progress 0.17) still leave the track every time, with max_error about 0.062-0.066 m against the 0.06 m off-track limit. The body-width term cannot raise that limit (it is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which stays at 0.06 for any allowed body), so tracking error on sharp alternating bends has to fall. Oval steering_oscillation of 0.33 is moderate, so the robot is not badly jittering there. Hypothesis H3: on tight, alternating bends the robot is too fast and too slow to respond, so it cuts past the line. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.4 to 1.2, giving more time to correct on bends. The oval has time headroom (1.69 s, limit 3 s), so this should still finish. (2) kp 1.6 to 2.0, for a stronger correction on sharp bends. (3) kd 0.4 to 0.6, to damp the faster corrections. (4) Seven sensors at x = -0.045, -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03, 0.045 (spacing 15 mm, same +/-0.045 m span) with weights [-2, -1.33, -0.67, 0, 0.67, 1.33, 2]. This keeps the signal gain per metre of lateral error about the same as iteration 1 (about 44 per m) but gives finer position resolution, so the line is less likely to fall between sensors on the slalom. Geometry otherwise unchanged (mass 0.6, track 0.12, radius 0.03, body 0.12 x 0.16). Expected result: slalom and s-bend progress rising well above 0.17 and 0.42, with some completions on the s-bend, and max_error nearer 0.05 m. Risk: kd 0.6 might add jitter, and the slower speed could push the oval close to the 3 s limit. Next measurements wanted: completion_time and progress per track, max_error and line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom, and steering_oscillation to check whether the extra kd causes jitter.
